metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Chile agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Kim, have you considered the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th? I think it could work well for everyone involved. 

Also, I’ve been curious about your thoughts on army rule. In my perspective, it’s not necessarily a bad thing, and I think it provides stability. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 4th sounds... okay, but we should also check if everyone can make it. I mean, it’s a busy time of year. 

As for army rule, I have to say that I believe it's a bad thing. In Chile, we experienced it firsthand, and it caused a lot of suffering. Stability shouldn't come at the cost of people's rights and freedoms.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand checking availability is important... but I really think January 4th is a good option. It gives us time to assess everything before moving forward.

Regarding army rule, I see your point about rights and freedoms. However, in my view, some level of control can actually foster stability and progress. It’s a complex situation, don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I see what you're saying about January 4th, and it’s good to be on the same page about timing. It might work well if everyone agrees.

When it comes to army rule, I think it’s interesting how we can have different views. I mean, deep down, we are all the same. We all want stability and progress, right? People are pretty much motivated by the same things. It's just that the way we see it can differ based on our experiences. But we both know, at the end of the day, it's about finding what works best for people.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

Regarding army rule, I still really believe it's not a good approach. Stability and development should come from democratic processes, not military control. That's crucial.
